speaker: Doctor
text:
A normal colonoscopy with biopsy is a crucial finding that effectively rules out colorectal cancer and significant mucosal lesions. Since the mass is palpable but the mucosa appears normal, could you describe the location of the mass more precisely—specifically, is it located in the anterior wall of the vagina or the posterior wall of the rectum?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal transrectal ultrasound suggests the mass is not within the rectal wall itself, pointing toward a lesion originating from adjacent structures like the vagina. Given your history of vaginal deliveries, could you clarify if the mass protrudes into the vaginal canal or if you have noticed any bulging in the vaginal area during exertion?

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal pelvic MRI is surprising given the palpable mass, suggesting it may be a superficial or very small lesion not easily visualized, or perhaps an external hemorrhoid. Since the mass is palpable but imaging is unrevealing, I will proceed with a definitive diagnosis based on the clinical presentation of a painless, palpable rectal mass in a woman with multiple vaginal deliveries.
